claims.statement: DORA applies from 17 January 2025 and requires in-scope financial entities to maintain and update registers of ICT third-party contractual arrangements.
The adopted ITS defines linked templates for entities, contracts, services, functions, providers, subcontractors, processing locations and other controlled fields.
Only 6.5% of analysed dry-run registers passed all data-quality checks; half of the remainder failed fewer than 5 of 116 checks.
A final Joint ESAs Q&A states that every financial entity subject to DORA must maintain a register, including entities using simplified ICT-risk treatment.
The ESAs used collected registers to designate critical ICT third-party providers in November 2025, showing that reporting is operational rather than hypothetical.
DoraGuard publishes EUR 1500 yearly for up to 20 ICT vendors, EUR 4999 for up to 100, and EUR 12500 for groups.
ReportAct publishes EUR 299 monthly per location plus a supplier fee, while Venvera publishes EUR 799 monthly for broader compliance including register export and contract clause checking.

contrary_evidence: Multiple products already provide validation and regulator-ready exports at transparent prices.
Venvera already combines register export with contract-clause checking, directly overlapping the proposed upstream wedge.
The official dry run found most submissions close to passing even though few passed every check, suggesting remediation may be episodic rather than a large permanent budget.
Smaller entities have fewer providers and proportionate requirements, limiting revenue per customer.
The vendor itself becomes an ICT third party requiring security, contractual and register treatment by clients.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: contractually permitted clause-to-cell mappings and recurrent validation-defect patterns, with customer data segregated and public rules treated as non-exclusive
fingerprint.customer: small and mid-sized EU payment, e-money, insurance and investment groups plus compliance outsourcers maintaining several DORA registers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: DORA consultancies, managed-service providers, specialist legal firms and failed-validation remediation engagements
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: secure contract extraction, controlled taxonomy, graph reconciliation, cell-level evidence, human approval, validation-rule checks and xBRL-CSV export
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: a regulated group or compliance partner pays onboarding and recurring fees per managed register workspace and vendor-contract inventory
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a contract, provider, subcontractor, entity, function, processing location or reporting validation changes

founder_fit: Strong fit for knowledge graphs, document AI, validation and quantitative quality control.
A Polish payments or insurance partner provides a bounded EU entry without camera-led distribution.
Financial-sector security, procurement and domain accountability cannot be handled casually alongside a full-time job; specialist review and support must be delegated.
A remediation pilot on customer-controlled or EU-hosted infrastructure is more founder-compatible than immediate full SaaS.
risks: Extraction errors can propagate into regulatory reporting unless every value is human-approved.
Confidential contracts and provider data create material security and access-control obligations.
Low-cost competitors can commoditize validation and xBRL-CSV generation.
Regulated customers remain accountable and may prefer established GRC suites or consultants.
Financial-sector procurement and incident response may exceed a part-time founder's capacity.
A public-rule corpus is not a moat; only permissioned defect and mapping data can compound.

structure.control_point: the human-approved register dataset, validation result and cell-level source provenance before submission
structure.critical_dependency: complete contract inventories, secure access, accurate hierarchies and enough upstream automation advantage over inexpensive DORA-native competitors

thesis: Convert ICT contracts, entity perimeters, functions and subcontractor chains into a human-approved DORA Register of Information with cell-level provenance, reconciliation and regulator-format exports. The rule is live and official dry-run evidence shows data-quality difficulty, but many priced products already generate the register. The differentiated wedge is contract ingestion, defect remediation and multi-client compliance-partner workflow, not a standalone spreadsheet formatter.
title: DORA Contract-to-Register Provenance Workspace
uncertainties: Paid demand for cell-level contract provenance beyond incumbent validation and export.
Partner access to confidential contracts and willingness to use a new vendor.
Actual frequency and cost of register updates and failed submissions.
Security certification, deployment and procurement requirements by segment.
Extraction accuracy across languages, amendments, framework contracts and subcontractors.
Partner channel commitment, support load and achievable retention.
